title: SEPARATION SYSTEM FOR STACKED HIGH ASPECT RATIO SATCOM SATELLITES ( ON REQUEST) (ARTES AT 4E.099) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and verify an Open Standard of a separation system specifically for stackedhigh aspect ratio satellites (up to 1,200 kg class spacecraft).Targeted Improvements:Enabling technology for launches of stackedhigh aspect ratio satellites.Description: High aspect ratio satellites are an established form factor for satcom satellites, already operating and providing global telecommunication services. To maximise launch capacity, it is common to launch large stacks of multiple (10s) of such satellites together. The required separation technologies have to date been bespoke developments by and for eachspecific constellation. In Europe, there is currently no such system available, nor an off the shelf existing solution.This activity aims to develop an open standard for a European hold down and release system to enable stacked launches of up to 60 high aspectratio (up to 1200kg class) satellites. This will ensure that development of such systems is coordinated across Europe and allow different providers to be mixed within single launches and across multiplelaunches and constellations. A separation system by necessity includes: a mechanical load path for the stack, the hold down mechanism, a pre-loading device to ensure that the stack is effectivelyheld down through launch conditions. a release mechanism and a sequencing system to control the ejection of each spacecraft fromthestack. The engineeringmodel separation system concept will be developed, and a breadboard will be manufactured and tested in asufficiently representative scenario to validate critical functions of the system in the different stacking configurations. Then, an engineering model will be manufactured and tested, including a series of deployment tests in different conditions to assessthe overalldesign performance. The final stage of the activity will propose an open standard for separation system for stacked high aspect ratio satcom satellites to promote compatibility of spacecraft design.

title: RECEIVER TECHNIQUES AND ALGORITHMS FOR PNT SOLUTIONS WITH ONLY 1 AND 2 LEO SATELLITES IN VIEW - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view, based on the optimised fusion ofall the available estimations along time.Description: The use of LEO-based systems on top of current GNSS systems (in MEO orbits) is being considered to improve the achievable user performances, in particular in challenging user scenarios. To ensure that at least3 or 4 satellites are in view by any user on ground, a much larger number of LEO satellites than for MEO is required to be used inthis case. In this context, it is of high interest to investigate techniques exploiting signals received by LEO satellites when only 1 and 2 LEO satellites are in view by a ground user. This would enable, for example, to exploit LEO satellites with reduced constellations with a limited available number of satellites visible, and/or while a full LEO-PNT constellation is still being deployed. Theobjective of this activity is to design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view,, including transitions between 1 and 2 satellites, based on the optimised fusion of all the available estimations along time, including at least:- ToA (Time-of-Arrival), FoA (Frequency-of-Arrival) and AoA (Angle-of-Arrival)-like estimations; - Multi-epoch / synthetic apertureprocessing solutions exploiting the fast satellite geometry change; and, additionally, if introducing benefits to the above : - Clock coasting; - Inertial sensors measurements; - DEM (Digital Elevation Model)/height sensors ; The suitability of the proposed solutions is aimed to be assessed based both on simulations and real data. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define and design innovative techniques and algorithms in the areas identified above; - Develop the required tools/software for the assessment/test of the innovative techniques and algorithms; - Assess/test the different techniques and algorithms in realistic simulated conditions, and with real signals from LEO satellites; - Identify the most promising techniques/algorithms based on the results obtained;- Propose the way-forward to further mature each of the promising techniques/algorithms identified.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. title: Sentinel and Landsat satellite data API
description: We are seeking for a provider of a Cloud API service for online satellite data archive and processing framework containing the following satellite platforms: Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 (L1C and L2A), Sentinel-3, Landsat-5, Landsat-7, Landsat-8 and Envisat MERIS.
